input.question: Why would you plead no contest in court?
input.ground_truth: No contest means that you cede to the sentence in good faith, which means that the sentence will have less of an impact on your record than losing a plead of not guilty. It's also a component of plea bargains, as it allows you to bargain down to a lesser sentence than if you were found guilty because you agree to the terms of the sentencing.

Question: Why would you plead no contest in court?

Okay! Imagine you did something that you're not supposed to do, like breaking a rule at school. If you "plead no contest," it means you’re not saying “I did it” or “I didn’t do it,” but you’re also not fighting the punishment. You’re saying, “I don’t want to argue. You can give me the punishment if that’s what you think is right.”

So, you admit you don’t want to say you’re innocent, but you also don’t say you’re guilty. You just let the judge decide what happens next.
